01 / A little about me

I’m interested in how
robots understand the world.

Taehyoung Kim.

I’m a Research Engineer at Fraunhofer IVI, working on perception systems for autonomous aerial robots. My research spans video understanding, multimodal sensing, and semantic 3D mapping.

I’m interested in the space between a promising research idea and a system that works beyond the benchmark. This site brings together my publications, experiments, and, over time, notes on what I’m learning and building.

More about my background ↗

02 / What I’ve been working on

Recent activity.

Recent papers and project updates. A small record of what I’m working on and sharing.

  1. Oct 2026

    Publication

    MultiFly preprint ↗

    A real-world aerial dataset connecting RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar through geometry-driven semantic label transfer.

  2. Sept 2026

    Publication

    VoxelFix preprint ↗

    Graph-based correction of semantic labels in completed voxel maps, keeping geometry and occupancy fixed.

  3. Jul 2026

    Publication

    MissionBench preprint ↗

    Mission-level evaluation of multimodal language-model agents for aerial tasks, including qualitative failure analysis.

  4. Jun 2026

    Publication

    FlexPath preprint ↗

    Learned semantic path priors connect image understanding with image-based planning.
